title: fix: prevent prompt drift and duplication during resize
body:
Resizing the terminal could move multiline prompts or leave duplicate lines behind. This fix prevents old prompt text from wrapping before the shell redraws it and leaves the screen unchanged if resizing fails. It also preserves Powerlevel10k’s prompt-start marker and ensures shell redraws use the updated terminal size.

Adds regression tests for repeated resizing, full-width prompts, and last-line-only redraws.

Related discussions: [OSC 133 prompt duplication on resize (#13629)](https://github.com/ghostty-org/ghostty/discussions/13629) and [similar prompt duplication when resizing splits (#9903)](https://github.com/ghostty-org/ghostty/discussions/9903).

AI disclosure: GPT-6 Astra helped to debug the issue and fix it.

files.patch:
@@ -272,9 +272,14 @@ _ghostty_deferred_init() {
     # We use 133;P instead of 133;A to avoid fresh-line behavior which would
     # disrupt the display since the prompt has already been drawn. We also
     # emit 133;B to mark the input area, which is needed for click-to-move.
+    # Powerlevel10k can emit its own marks through prompt expansion, so they
+    # aren't necessarily literal bytes in PS1. In that case a fallback initial
+    # mark here would replace the start of its multiline prompt with the input
+    # row, leaving the earlier rows outside the region cleared on resize.
     (( $+functions[_ghostty_zle_line_init] )) || _ghostty_zle_line_init() { builtin true; }
     functions[_ghostty_zle_line_init]="
-        if [[ \$PS1 != *$'%{\\e]133;A'* ]]; then
+        if [[ \$PS1 != *$'%{\\e]133;A'* ]] &&
+           (( ! \${_POWERLEVEL9K_TERM_SHELL_INTEGRATION:-0} )); then
             builtin print -nu \$_ghostty_fd '\\e]133;P;k=i\\a\\e]133;B\\a'
         fi
     "${functions[_ghostty_zle_line_init]}
